title: Stand a birthday candle upright in each of three cupcakes, holding each soft cupcake by its rim without squashing it
instruction: Put one birthday candle in each of the three cupcakes so that it stands upright.
context: A cupcake weighs 45 g and gives under the fingers: held too hard it is squashed, not held it slides or tips, and a thin wax candle pushed crooked snaps, while one pushed in too shallow leans and falls over. Everyone knows the picture from birthdays at home and at school: cupcakes on a board, a candle standing in each. Here one hand holds each cupcake lightly by the rim of its icing cap while the other takes a candle out of a lump of Play-Doh in an egg cup, pushes it straight down through the icing until the cake holds it upright, and lets go. The cake holds the candle only by friction along it and a sideways hold that grows with depth, so a candle stands only if it went in deep enough and straight. Unlike RoboCasa's GarnishCupcake, where a garnish is set down on or beside a cake, here a slender, breakable thing is driven into a soft one while the other hand keeps the soft one still without crushing it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. A beech board 30 x 20 x 1.5 cm (630 g, loose), its middle at x 32.5, y -3, long side across. Three Hostess CupCakes (chocolate with the white loop of icing, sold in packs of two; 45 g; about 60 mm across the top, 50 mm at the base, 35 mm high; from a box opened the same day, kept at room temperature and within its best-by date), unwrapped, standing on the board in a row 3.5 cm from its near edge, 9 cm apart: x 26, y +6, -3 and -12. A porcelain egg cup on a foot (dark green, 45 mm across inside) filled with one 2 oz can of yellow Play-Doh, at x 42, y -25, holding four Wilton 2 1/2 in birthday candles (63 x 5 mm, about 1 g; two blue, two red) upright and 15 mm deep at the corners of a 22 mm square; one is a spare. By seed the row moves up to 1 cm along the board's edge and each cupcake up to 7 mm in any direction; seed 0 is the layout above. Everything else is fixed. Gripper pads in nitrile finger cots. Start check: cupcakes on marks on the board and board and cup on marks on the bench (within 2 mm), a photo from above. Squeeze camera (bench only): a camera on a fixed mount beyond the board at x 60, y -3, its lens about 45 mm over the bench, level with the cupcakes' rims, looking straight back towards the arms; it sees the three rims edge-on and both pads of the gripper that steadies a cupcake, the pushing hand working above the rims and the egg cup off its line of sight. Before the trials a millimetre scale stood upright at the middle cupcake's place, in the rims' plane, is filmed to give the pixels per millimetre there (about 6 with a 1080p camera and a 30 cm wide view); the camera is not moved afterwards.
scoring: Read from the end state. 1.0: each cupcake carries one candle standing by itself, at most 10 degrees off the vertical, at least 12 mm deep (at most 51 mm showing) and within 12 mm of the middle of its top; no cupcake squashed (the steadying gripper's pads closed 4 mm or more past first touch on its rim), none off the board or tilted 30 degrees or more; no candle snapped; both grippers clear (the point between each gripper's pads at least 6 cm from the middle of every cupcake's top and 7 cm from the lower end of every candle in a cupcake); cupcakes and candles at rest (under 5 mm/s and 0.05 rad/s). 0.75: the same with one flaw: one candle leaning 10 to 25 degrees, or less than 12 mm deep but standing, or off the middle; or one candle snapped and the spare used. 0.5: two cupcakes as for full score. 0.25: one. 0: less; or two or more cupcakes squashed or off the board. A candle counts in a cupcake while the cupcake holds it and it leans 25 degrees or less; two candles in one cupcake count for none. Real bench: a photo from the side of each cupcake against a set square for the lean, a rule for the height showing, and for the squeeze a calibrated video from the fixed rim camera (setup): the gap between the inner faces of the steadying gripper's pads is read frame by frame in millimetres, and a cupcake counts as squashed when that gap has fallen 4 mm or more under the gap at first touch on its rim, the same closing the simulation scores; the video also shows a snapped candle.
reset_notes: Three fresh cupcakes from a box opened the same day, at room temperature, on their marks; every candle that was used is replaced by a new one from the box, the Play-Doh lump pressed level again and the four candles stood 15 mm deep at its marks; finger cots changed; board and egg cup on their marks. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at true size. A cupcake has a soft contact (4 N at 4 mm of closing at its rim) and is swapped for a squashed shape past 4 mm. A candle is two pieces on a bending spring that snaps at 0.02 N m, held in the cake by capped friction along it and a sideways spring rising with depth, torn out past 25 degrees; it weighs 10 g with 9 g of that carried, for the solver. Values assumed until a kitchen test. Not modelled: icing cracking, crumbs, wax smearing.
